title: Mary's Tavern with drummer George Williams after the Navy
summary: His first regular job after the service paid five dollars a night plus the kitty.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Years later, but that was before I went to the service. Right. That was before I went to the service. And when I got out of the service, I went back to school. And I was working at a club they called Mary's Tavern on a magazine near Jackson Avenue. Nice.

And see, when I came out of the Navy, and the guy George Williams, drummer, he called me up in the morning to play every night with him. I said, well, how much is a job paying? And when he told me how much the job was paying, I said, yes, indeed. Because see, when I left away from him, we were getting a dollar and a half a night. Yeah. And on some of the jobs, like we played some of those big country clubs, we'd get three dollars a piece. So when I started working at Mary's Tavern, when I got out of the Navy in Georgia, I asked me to work with him, I said, well, how much is the job paying? He said, five dollars a night. Five dollars a night. He said, we passed the kitty. And we passed the kitty, man, we would make it but five dollars a piece every night in the kitty.
So that would be almost ten dollars.
Yeah. You see, I was married and I had my family to take care of.
